item.title: Pakistan players 'more focused on earning money': Ex-chief selector claims
item.description: Former Pakistan spinner Iqbal Qasim criticised young cricketers for prioritising money and league contracts over improving skills and game awareness. He also questioned selectors’ lack of vision and warned against interference in cricket administration. Recalling his playing days, Qasim highlighted the importance of independent preparation, discipline and representing Pakistan, saying financial rewards naturally follow improved performance.

item.title: Months after Dells' $6.25Bn ‘gift’, US Treasury sets new Trump Account paycheck rules
item.description: New rules from the US Treasury and IRS will allow payroll contributions to Trump Accounts. Employers can contribute up to $2,500 tax-free annually for employees' dependent children. Employees will also have the option to make pre-tax paycheck contributions directly into these accounts. Michael and Susan Dell pledged $6.25 billion to fund this child savings initiative. The proposed regulations are now open for public comment before finalization.

item.title: Power struggle at Tata group deepens as N Chandrasekaran steps down
item.description: The battle for influence within the Tata Group after the death of former chairman Ratan Tata in 2024 has led to the exit of several senior leaders who were closely associated with him, altering the leadership dynamics at India's largest business conglomerate.

item.title: Why India wants 114 more Rafales and what gives the fighter its edge
item.description: Dassault Aviation from France has presented its proposal for acquiring 114 Rafale jets, aimed at strengthening India’s fighter fleet and addressing existing capability shortcomings. This initiative prioritizes significant local production and the transfer of technology to India. With a unified force of 176 Rafale aircraft, both the Indian Air Force and Navy will collaborate, enhancing India's domestic aerospace manufacturing and supporting indigenous defense projects.

item.title: Ex-Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer changes how his $8 billion philanthropy works
item.description: Steve and Connie Ballmer are redefining their charitable strategy. The Ballmer Group is set to detach three regional branches, allowing them to operate as independent nonprofits. This adaptation is designed to align funding strategies more closely with the needs of local communities. With over eight billion dollars donated to charity, the Ballmers will shift their emphasis toward national-level initiatives focusing on economic mobility.

item.title: 'Write Vishwavidyalaya in Hindi': UP minister's challenge to Rahul Gandhi
item.description: Uttar Pradesh Energy Minister AK Sharma challenged Rahul Gandhi's Hindi language skills. He questioned Gandhi's ability to write 'Vishwavidyalaya' and identify farm crops. Sharma also discussed Uttar Pradesh's bioenergy and smart meter initiatives. The state is a leading producer of compressed biogas and aims for more growth. Investors are invited to explore Uttar Pradesh's bioenergy sector opportunities.

item.title: Tennessee farmer refused $20 an acre for national park land: What happened next
item.description: In 1929, Tennessee farmer John W. Oliver refused to sell his 375-acre Cades Cove farm for $20 an acre, leading to a lengthy court battle over land wanted for Great Smoky Mountains National Park. After the Tennessee Supreme Court ruled against him, Oliver ultimately lost his property and received $17,000 in 1935.

item.title: Malaysia’s Princess Ilyana marries British GT racer Chris Froggatt
item.description: Tengku Puteri Raja Tengku Puteri Ilyana Alia, daughter of Pahang Sultan Al-Sultan Abdullah, married British racing driver Christopher Lionel Froggatt in Kuala Lumpur on August 7. The ceremony was attended by members of the Pahang royal family and followed traditional Islamic wedding customs, including the presentation of ‘mas kahwin’, ring exchange and ‘merenjis’.

item.title: Oracle layoffs: Company's '6 am layoff emails' may return in next few days
item.description: Oracle is preparing another round of layoffs this month, with cuts reaching double-digit percentages on some teams and managers already asked to name affected employees. The company wants payroll reduced before its second quarter starts on September 1. Oracle has already shed 21,000 jobs in a year, down to 141,000 staff, as it funds a debt-heavy AI data centre buildout that burned $23.7 billion in cash last fiscal year.

item.description: Maharashtra FDA suspended licenses of four Domino's Pizza outlets for hygiene violations. Action was taken against outlets in Mumbai and Satara districts. Inspections revealed deficiencies in cleanliness, storage, and pest control measures. A special drive covered 104 chain restaurants across Maharashtra. Overall, 11 food business licenses were suspended after inspections.

item.description: Actor Jr NTR has successfully completed shoulder surgery at KIMS Hospitals and conveyed heartfelt thanks to his fans, friends, and family for their support. The arthroscopic surgery was executed by a skilled team of orthopaedic surgeons. With an eye towards recovery, Jr NTR is now embarking on a supervised rehabilitation regimen, with doctors optimistic about his full recovery in the next two to three months.

item.title: Woman out for a drive with friend gangraped by 6 in Cuttack
item.description: A woman was allegedly gangraped by several men in Cuttack district on Tuesday night. The incident occurred when she and her friend stopped their vehicle near Sukarpada village. The suspects reportedly assaulted the male friend and then proceeded to assault the woman. Police have registered a case and formed multiple teams to apprehend the accused individuals. Authorities are hopeful for the swift arrest of the perpetrators involved in this crime.

item.title: Nolan Wells update: Friend blames mother for fueling backlash and threats after death
item.description: Jax Pitalo has accused Christine Wonsley of helping fuel the online backlash against him and two other friends after Nolan Wells’ death. Pitalo and Warren Hudson said the friends have faced threats and harassment after their identities became public. They deny involvement in Wells’ death and say they are considering legal action over false claims made about them.

item.description: Josh Kushner’s reported Lakers purchase has put his fortune and family back in focus. The Thrive Capital founder is married to Karlie Kloss and has three children. He is also the younger brother of Jared Kushner and the son of Charles Kushner. With a reported $5.2 billion net worth, his latest NBA deal marks a major new chapter.

item.title: Formula E signs landmark Disney+ deal to stream championship in 144 territories
item.description: Formula E is set for a major global push as Disney+ becomes the championship's new streaming home from the 2026/27 season. Under a new multi-year deal, fans in 144 territories will be able to watch every Formula E race weekend live on Disney+, including practice, qualifying and races. In the US, the championship will also stream on ESPN+, bringing the electric racing series to millions of new fans.

item.title: US removed 100 outdated dams, setting a new river restoration record
item.description: In 2025, the US removed 100 outdated and unsafe dams across 30 states, reconnecting more than 4,893 miles of rivers, the highest number of upstream river miles restored through dam removal in a single year. The projects reopened fish habitats, improved river connectivity and addressed public safety concerns. Pennsylvania led with 14 removals, followed by Massachusetts with 11 and Vermont with nine.

item.title: Mexico clears 100,000 tons of sargassum as seaweed crisis hits tourism
item.description: In 2026, a massive expanse of Sargassum seaweed has taken over the Atlantic Ocean, wreaking havoc on coastal areas. Mexico is facing an unprecedented surge in seaweed accumulation, which is damaging its tourism sector. The foul odor has led to a notable decline in visitors, leaving local businesses in distress. Though scientists predict improvement by late autumn, a permanent solution is still unknown.

Training in Hisar improved his throw by nearly 20 metres, despite a knee injury. However, his family’s financial struggles continue, and he is still seeking employment. Google's latest offerings focus on addressing user feedback and incorporating artificial intelligence.

item.title: Florida's 23-acre private island hits market for $12 million after 150 years
item.description: Nestled near Haines City, Florida, Bannon Island—a coveted private island—has hit the market after remaining in one family for four generations. The residence skillfully marries aged 19th-century cypress wood with contemporary glass elements. With additional buildings and lush landscapes, the potential for creative development is endless. It offers the perfect balance of tranquility and accessibility, keeping Orlando and Tampa just a short distance away.

item.title: Engineers turned dredged sediment into four new Columbia River islands
item.description: In an exciting environmental initiative, dredged sediment is being repurposed to form new islands aimed at habitat restoration. Engineers have meticulously placed this sediment to construct islands and adjacent channels along the river. Researchers are examining these man-made islands to gauge their impact on supporting wildlife, especially juvenile salmon. This pioneering technique may pave the way for future efforts in restoration ecology.

item.title: Who was Abbie Lainton? 16-year-old British cheerleader dies in boat accident
item.description: Abbie Lainton was a 16-year-old British cheerleader from Swindon who died after a boat accident during a family holiday in the Dominican Republic. She was known for cheerleading, dancing and her bright personality. Her siblings were also injured. Her family has received more than £22,000 through a fundraiser, while her former school and cheer team have paid tribute.
